add.notes: photo from Mark, 771 N. Crafford St., 2010. A brick foursquare with a hipped roof, a front gable dormer with two arched windows, white eaves and brackets, porches on brick piers, and white-trimmed windows. The address is 771 N. Crafford St. on dodsworthfh.com/location/bushnell and on legacy.com. The given coordinates, 40.554749, -90.505232, put it on the East Main side of Crafford, in the 700 block, Wells to Twyman. March 1906 sheet 5 and February 1912 sheet 7 draw blocks east of Wells, and those lots were not copied, so no Sanborn footprint was matched. The footprint is the photograph, and that is an estimate. No year-built was found, so the house is first drawn at the 1920 stop, and that start is an estimate. No family name is printed. The Martin-Hollis name is not painted on.

add.name: First Presbyterian Church

facade.photoSource: Postcard captioned First Presbyterian Church, Bushnell, Ill.

facadeSpec.citation: Postcard captioned First Presbyterian Church, Bushnell, Ill.

add.notes: The congregation's building was dedicated in 1869 on this ground and is the plainer church drawn through 1910. In May 1903 the old church, which faced north, was turned to face west on the corner lot, and dedicated again on 3 January 1904. The centennial book says the building was enlarged to its present size beginning in the spring of 1917, the Smith Memorial Hall work having started in the summer of 1916. The crenellated tower, pointed windows, and cross gables are that enlarged church, from Mark's postcard. The model has no 1917 stop, so the new front appears at the 1920 stop, the first one after the enlargement. The earlier building stays through 1910.

streets.name: Cole Street
streets.notes: The south leg of Cole Street, the highway, leaves the town Cole Street between Hail and Barnes and runs south to Murphy Road. It is drawn from 1920 because the 1918 Good Hope sheet already shows that road. The 1974 Bushnell West sheet labels the street Cole and draws the same south leg. The line meets the grid because Hail, Hurst, Barnes, Davis, Gridley, Wells, and Twyman are extended to Cole Street from 1880. The ribbon width is not a surveyed right-of-way.

streets.name: Murphy Road
streets.notes: The east-west road at the south edge of town where Cole Street's highway meets it. OpenStreetMap calls the road Murphy Road. The 1918 Good Hope sheet draws this crossing. The longer run of Murphy Road toward Lakelawn is on the 1944 Avon sheet and is shown from 1950. The ribbon width is not a surveyed right-of-way.
